note.question: How do store-brand introduction and multilateral contracting interact?
note.overview: We explore the impacts of store-brand (SB) introduction on multilateral contracting in vertical supply relationships that involve two upstream national-brand manufacturers (NBMs) selling through a common retailer. Two different information structures are scrutinized: simultaneous (secret offers) versus sequential contracting (public offers), essentially different timing by which the NBMs contract with the retailer. SB products are prevalent nowadays; however, the market shares in different categories vary substantially, from negligible sales (e.g., alcoholic beverages) to more than half of the total sales (e.g., milk).

source.quote: In a common retailer setting, Shang et al. (2016) show that the retailer prefers to sell private demand information to the manufacturers sequentially rather than simultaneously, whereas the manufacturers’ preferences are reversed.
